the expression of the iron-regulatory peptide hormone hepcidine increases in cardiomyocites under myocarditis and infarction.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of hepcidins in the heart and the kinetics of altered expression in diseases of this organ.

the kinetics of altered expression of hepcidine, a peptide hormone that is thought to play an important role as an iron regulator, in rat experimental autoimmune mycarditis, rat acute myocardial injury, and human myocarditis.
the role of iron in myocardial diseases and the possible involvement of iron in the pathogenesis of these diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hepcidins in the heart are induced by inflammatory cytokines in myocarditis and MI.
hepcidin and ferroportin are up-regulated in the heart in response to inflammatory cytokine stimulation and that hepcidins are induced in cardiomyocyte cells under myocarditis and in infarction.
hepcidin may have a role in the pathophysiology of myocarditis and myocardium infarction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hepcidin may be a new marker for inflammatory diseases of the heart.
hepcidin plays a role in the pathophysiological processes of myocarditis and MI.
iron metabolism is closely related to myocarditis and MI.

the peptide hormone hepidin is strongly induced under inflammatory conditions and in infarction.
hepcidin may be a potential therapeutic target for myocarditis and AMI.
